h1: SEO cost in India: what ₹10,000, ₹40,000 and ₹1,50,000 each buy
metaTitle: SEO Cost in India 2026: Price Bands That Are Real
metaDescription: SEO cost in India runs from ₹8,000 to ₹3,00,000 a month. We map every band to headcount, deliverables and the outcome it can honestly be expected to hit.
answer: SEO in India costs ₹8,000 to ₹3,00,000 a month. The useful way to read that range is headcount: roughly 55% of a retainer reaches delivery salaries, and a junior SEO executive costs about ₹45,000 a month fully loaded. So under ₹25,000 you're funding less than one junior, part-time.
takeaways: Convert the fee into people. Multiply the retainer by 0.55, then divide by what the role costs. The answer is usually smaller than the pitch implied.
**₹25,000 a month is the line below which nobody can staff a full junior on your account.** Not a judgement — payroll arithmetic.
Indian rates run 60–75% under US rates because salaries and rent are lower, not because the work is. Google's index has no idea where the crawl was run from.
Tools are priced in dollars and cost the same in Chennai as in Chicago, so software eats a far bigger share of a ₹40,000 retainer than a $4,000 one. Cheap retainers cut tools first.

sections.h2: Read every quote as a headcount, not a price
body: A retainer is a payroll line wearing a nicer outfit. Somebody's salary, some software, some overhead, some margin. If you can work out how much of your fee turns into a person, you can work out what the month will contain — before you sign anything.

Of every ₹100 you send an Indian agency, roughly ₹25–30 goes on software licences, admin, sales, and the bench time between clients. Another ₹15–20 is margin, which is normal and necessary — an agency with no margin has no ability to fix its own mistakes. That leaves **₹50–60 that reaches the people doing your work**, and 55% is a fair working number.
Then you need what those people cost. These are the fully loaded monthly costs — salary plus PF, gratuity, insurance, a laptop, a seat, and the honest fact that nobody bills every working hour.
bullets: **Junior SEO executive** — ₹40,000–₹50,000 a month, fully loaded. Can execute a checklist. Cannot decide what goes on it.
**Mid-level specialist** (technical, content or outreach) — ₹90,000–₹1,20,000. Owns one discipline properly.
**Senior strategist or lead** — ₹1,70,000–₹2,20,000. The person who's already seen your problem happen to somebody else.

callout.title: Where these numbers come from
callout.body: These are the bands Indian agencies hire in, loaded for statutory costs and non-billable time. They swing ±30% by city — a lead in Bengaluru costs meaningfully more than the same lead in Indore. Treat them as a sanity check on a quote, not a payroll table.

sections.h2: Why Indian rates sit 60–75% below US and UK rates
body: This is the question every overseas buyer asks and every Indian founder should understand, because it's the same gap read from two directions.

A US agency quoting $3,000 a month is quoting roughly ₹2.5–₹2.7 lakh, depending on the rate that week. That's not their premium tier — in many US markets it's the entry point. The same scope in India is quoted at ₹75,000. The difference is almost entirely salary and rent, plus the cost of a US sales function that has to be funded by the retainer.

None of that makes the output worse. Google's crawler doesn't know which city rendered the page, and a canonical tag written in Pune behaves exactly like one written in Portland. Indian teams have been doing English-language technical SEO for global clients for two decades.
There are two honest counterweights, though, and cheap agencies exploit both.
numbered: **Tools are priced in dollars.** Ahrefs, Semrush, Screaming Frog, a rank tracker and a log analyser cost the same in Coimbatore as in Chicago. On a $4,000 retainer that's a rounding error. On a ₹40,000 one it's a large, visible line — which is exactly why the cheapest Indian retainers quietly run without crawl data or backlink data. A team without either is guessing with confidence.

**The gap narrows at the top.** Indian agencies serving US and UK clients compete for the same senior people as everyone else, so their rates converge with international ones. If you're paying international prices, ask where the team physically sits — [Indian agency versus international agency](/compare/indian-seo-agency-vs-international-agency) covers what actually changes.

sections.h2: GST, TDS, and the two numbers that aren't on the quote
body: Indian agency pricing has a habit of arriving as one number and invoicing as another. Neither of these is a trick — but nobody mentions them in the pitch.

**GST is 18%**, and virtually every Indian agency quotes exclusive of it. A ₹75,000 retainer bills at ₹88,500. If your business is GST-registered, that's input credit and therefore a cash-flow cost rather than a real one. If you're below the registration threshold — plenty of clinics, coaching centres and small proprietorships are — it's a genuine 18% on top, and you should be budgeting ₹88,500 from the start.

**TDS applies too.** Indian companies deduct tax at source on agency invoices, commonly at 2% or 10% depending on how the service gets classified. It doesn't change what you pay in total, but it does change the cheque, and it catches out first-time buyers who assumed the invoice number was the transfer number. Your CA will tell you which section applies to your contract.
If you're an overseas client buying from an Indian agency, export of services can be zero-rated under an LUT. Ask before you assume 18% — it's a large enough sum to be worth one email.

sections.h2: Freelancer, boutique, or a team of four
body: The same site gets wildly different quotes because it's being quoted by wildly different businesses. Here's what each type genuinely costs in India and where each one wins.
bullets: **Freelancer — ₹15,000–₹60,000/mo.** No office, no sales team, no bench, so far more of your fee becomes work. Almost always one strong discipline and two weak ones. Wins clearly below ₹40,000. Fails on breadth, and on the fortnight they're unwell or chasing a bigger client.

**Boutique agency, three to ten people — ₹40,000–₹1,25,000/mo.** Two or three disciplines covered, the founder still touches the work, and you can get them on a call. The sweet spot for local businesses and small national sites.

**Multi-discipline agency, 25+ people — ₹75,000–₹5,00,000/mo.** All four disciplines, real process, and a documented handover when someone leaves. Also the highest risk that the people who won the pitch never appear again.

**An overseas agency's Indian delivery arm — quoted in dollars, delivered from India.** Perfectly legitimate. Just know you're paying international rates for the cost base described above, and ask directly where the team sits.

callout.title: The comparison that actually works
callout.body: Ask all three for the same thing: hours per month, split by role, and the tool licences they'll run on your account. The quotes stop being comparable on price and start being comparable on substance. [What an SEO agency costs](/cost/seo-agency-cost) runs the same exercise in hours instead of headcount.

sections.h2: What we charge, and what the number is attached to
body: So you can hold us against the table above rather than taking it on trust.

SEO runs **from ₹75,000/mo**, and smaller sites from **₹40,000/mo**. Organic Social & Content is ₹30,000, ₹50,000 or ₹70,000 a month. Performance Marketing is ₹40,000, ₹75,000 or ₹1,50,000 a month. Bundled: SEO plus social is ₹99,000/mo, social plus performance is ₹75,000/mo, all three is ₹1,75,000/mo. All ex-GST. Ad spend is billed separately with zero media markup.

The price isn't the interesting part. What it's attached to is. On day one we freeze your trailing-90-day count of qualified leads from organic search — written down, agreed, before anyone touches the site. If we haven't beaten that number in 90 days, we keep working free until we do.

We never promise a specific ranking position for a specific keyword. Nobody controls Google's index, and an agency that claims otherwise is quoting you a coin flip with a straight face. We promise movement against **your own** baseline, which is the only number that pays anybody's salary.

It's also why we take three new clients a month and no more. You can't carry that risk at volume — and every agency that says it can is relying on you not measuring. The current rate card lives on [our pricing page](/pricing).

faqs.q: How much does SEO cost per month in India?
faqs.a: Quotes cluster between ₹8,000 and ₹3,00,000 a month, ex-GST. A local site under 30 pages has a genuine starting line around ₹25,000–₹40,000. A competitive national keyword set needs ₹75,000–₹1,50,000, because that's the first band that funds four disciplines at once.

faqs.q: Is ₹10,000 a month enough for SEO in India?
faqs.a: Not for a programme. At 55% of the fee reaching salaries, ₹10,000 buys about ₹5,500 of somebody's time — roughly a tenth of a junior executive's month. That's enough for a report and a few meta tags. Spend it on one useful thing instead, or save it toward one proper audit.

faqs.q: Why do two Indian agencies quote so differently for the same website?
faqs.a: Because they're quoting different amounts of work and rarely saying so out loud. One quote includes four researched articles, technical implementation and outreach; the other includes a monthly PDF and title tag edits. Ask both for hours by role plus the tool licences they'll use, and the gap explains itself in about a minute.

faqs.q: Is GST charged on SEO services in India?
faqs.a: Yes, at 18%, and almost every agency quotes ex-GST. A ₹75,000 retainer invoices at ₹88,500. GST-registered businesses can claim input credit, so it's a cash-flow cost. If you're not registered, it's a real 18% and belongs in your budget from day one.

faqs.q: Are Indian SEO agencies worse than US or UK ones?
faqs.a: The price gap is salaries and rent, not competence — Indian teams have done English-language technical SEO for global clients for twenty years. The real risk is different: cheap Indian retainers cut dollar-priced tools first, so check the licences on your account before you check anything else.

faqs.q: What is a realistic first-year SEO budget for an Indian business?
faqs.a: For a small local business, ₹40,000 a month plus a one-off audit — roughly ₹5,00,000 for the year including GST. For a competitive national set, ₹75,000–₹1,50,000 a month, so ₹10,00,000–₹20,00,000. Budget twelve months, not three; nothing compounds inside a quarter.
